tasks.short: Observe equipment and cloth, judge correct operation and record relevant findings.

steps.what: Retrieve the current process specification and equipment operating references
Observe display screens, control panels, equipment and cloth entering or exiting processes
Determine whether equipment operation and cloth behaviour are correct
Record equipment observation findings and relevant batch context

tasks.design: Configure a batch specification view and observation fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Physical inspection and the decision about correct operation remain human, with observation writing separately priced rather than folded into inspection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Process reference navigation and observation formatting interrupt direct monitoring.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch views and observation fields can reduce those clerical portions.
tasks.still_hard: Cloth behaviour, sound, vibration and conditions not represented on a display.
tasks.human_edge: The operator combines equipment readings with physical observation.
tasks.altitude: Reduce reference and record handling around direct equipment observation.

reach.learn: Keep physical findings attached to batch context

evidence.claim: Lectra Valia provides production and maintenance dashboards for adjacent textile processes, not a demonstrated dyeing inspection result.
The proposed batch-view and observation-field benefit is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Includes reference lookup and existing observation records alongside physical monitoring; no new mandatory record is introduced to create savings.
Operator produces batch ID, machine ID, observation time and equipment/cloth finding in s1-s4, with capture time counted. Missing process reference or uncertain condition requires manual checking.
Native view and record fields first; no added sensor, machine vision, automatic alert or process adjustment.
Ordinary record saves remain retained and ungated; malfunction notification belongs to task 14122.
unknowns: Existing observation record practice and batch reference access
research_questions: Are findings currently written separately and which fields are repeated?

incremental.description: Maintain batch view and observation fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=95, gross=5, upkeep=1, central net=4 E1. Low: paper-only batch specifications and bespoke observation notes prevent most reuse, retaining 99 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: stable batch IDs improve lookup and some note fields while physical interpretation remains full, retaining 97 hours plus upkeep for 2 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notify colleagues of machine malfunctions and separately write the fault record.

steps.what: Identify the malfunction symptoms, machine and immediate operational concern
Retrieve the responsible supervisor or mechanic contact
Check fault facts and notify supervisors or mechanics of equipment malfunctions
Write the malfunction record, symptoms and notification details
Clarify the malfunction and response requirements with the maintenance colleague

tasks.design: Use a current maintenance-contact view and native fault form in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Immediate notification remains a checked human call, followed by a separate fault record; the form does not delay urgent communication or imply an automated send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact lookup and repeated escalation fields add handling around the call.
tasks.enabler_now: Native contact views and fault fields can reduce repeated record work.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising urgency and explaining actual symptoms.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can communicate immediate conditions and answer clarifying questions.
tasks.altitude: Make the fault record easier while preserving prompt human notification.

reach.learn: Capture symptoms without inventing a diagnosis

evidence.claim: Native contact views and fault forms can reduce repeated lookup and escalation writing; no measured local benefit is supplied.

assumptions: Includes the maintenance escalation write as a distinct step after immediate notification; it is not hidden inside the phone call.

Operator produces machine ID, symptom, time, batch and urgency facts in s1 and records them with contact and call details in s4, with capture priced. Missing contacts use the established manual escalation route.
Native contact roster and fault template first; no automatic diagnosis, alert or message action.
Ordinary fault saves are retained without self-approval. Notification goes to colleagues, so authority is write_internal.
unknowns: Current fault record structure and contact roster reliability
research_questions: How much fault writing repeats machine and batch identifiers?

already_counted.description: Capture fault symptoms and notification details

incremental.description: Maintain contact view and fault fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact machine identity, symptoms and immediate concern communicated to the current responsible colleague; changed facts require checking before notification.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=91.5, gross=8.5, upkeep=1.5, central net=7 E1. Low: unlisted equipment and unusual symptoms force a bespoke fault note, retaining 98.5 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: recognised machine IDs populate some fields but symptom description and urgency remain manual, retaining 94.5 hours plus upkeep for 4 net.

tasks.short: Monitor dyeing temperatures and flows, compare captured readings with limits and assess deviations.

steps.what: Retrieve the specified temperature and dye flow ranges for the batch
Capture the batch-specific range limits, units and observation interval
Read and record temperatures and dye flow rates from existing instruments
Compare captured temperatures and flow rates against the specified ranges
Assess range deviations, instrument reliability and process implications
Record process monitoring findings and any unresolved deviation

tasks.design: Use the native recipe view in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a checked range-comparison sheet in {SPREADSHEET}. The operator captures limits and readings; a separate deterministic comparison displays results, while interpretation and monitoring records remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual comparison of readings with recipe limits consumes monitoring effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing formulas can compare explicitly captured values and limits consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Bad instruments, wrong recipes and process behaviour despite in-range values.
tasks.human_edge: The operator checks whether the readings and comparison make physical sense.
tasks.altitude: Reduce arithmetic comparison while preserving physical process awareness.

reach.learn: Verify units and recipe identity before comparison

evidence.claim: Deterministic formulas can compare captured readings against explicit limits; no measured dyeing labour benefit is supplied.

assumptions: Counts recipe lookup, limit capture, instrument reading and recording, comparison, judgement and monitoring record.

Operator produces batch, lower/upper limit, unit and interval in s2 and timestamped measured values in s3, with capture fully priced. Instruments produce the existing display values. Missing units, absent limits or uncertain readings stop comparison for manual checking.
Native panel comparison first: if already configured, retain existing operation and claim no new comparison saving. Sheet scenario applies only to current manual comparisons.
s4 displays results only; no hidden out-of-range send, alarm or machine adjustment is named. Ordinary record saves remain retained and ungated.
unknowns: Existing panel limit displays and present comparison effort
research_questions: Do operators actually compare manually or already use native range indicators?

already_counted.description: Capture and verify the comparison limits

incremental.description: Maintain comparison formulas and test recipe changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=66, gross=34, upkeep=5, central net=29 E1. Low: incompatible recipe units and unstable readings require frequent manual reconciliation, retaining 92 hours plus upkeep for 3 net. High: consistent recipe metadata permits formula comparisons but unusual transitions retain extra monitoring, retaining 77 hours plus upkeep for 18 net. If native range comparison already performs the work, its existing benefit is excluded entirely.

tasks.short: Clarify order and processing issues with coworkers and separately record the agreed understanding.

steps.what: Identify the order details, processing plans or problems needing clarification
Retrieve the current order details and processing plan references
Confer with coworkers to resolve order, processing or problem information gaps
Write the order clarification, processing decision and unresolved issue note

tasks.design: Configure current-order views and short processing clarification fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Coworker discussion stays human, while order lookup and the separate written clarification receive their own effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scattered order references and repeated note structure add handling around clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and note templates can reduce that clerical work.
tasks.still_hard: Tacit process knowledge and ambiguous or changing order details.
tasks.human_edge: Coworkers explain what happened and whether the written plan fits reality.
tasks.altitude: Reduce information handling while retaining direct shop-floor understanding.

reach.learn: Attach decisions to current order versions

evidence.claim: Native order views and clarification fields can reduce repeated lookup and note formatting; this benefit is unmeasured.

assumptions: Includes actual order lookup and any existing clarification record; neither is hidden inside the coworker conversation.
Operator produces order/batch ID, plan version, clarification and unresolved issue in s4, with capture priced. Conflicting versions or uncertain facts require direct manual clarification.
Native views and note fields first; no automatic order change, supervisor approval or hidden message.
Ordinary record save remains retained without self-approval; no new note requirement is created solely for savings.
unknowns: Existing clarification record practice and order version quality
research_questions: Which clarifications require a record and how much writing is repeated structure?
